summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, multiple prior stents, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, type 2 diabetes, and antiphospholipid syndrome presented with chest pain during a scheduled endoscopy, found to have an aborted inferior STEMI. Initial evaluation showed subtherapeutic INR of 1.4 and normal initial troponin, which later peaked at 0.16. Coronary angiography revealed stable coronary anatomy with no new intervenable lesions. He was managed with heparin infusion and transitioned to warfarin 6 mg daily, with continuation of dual antiplatelet therapy. His metoprolol was reduced to 150 mg and valsartan to 80 mg due to orthostasis, and diltiazem was discontinued. Insulin was adjusted for glucose control. He remained stable, with INR reaching 2.5 at discharge. He was discharged home on optimized medical therapy with follow-up planned in primary care, cardiology, and anticoagulation clinics.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unspecified angina pectoris
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with unspecified diabetic retinopathy without macular edema
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
